title: Buoyancy under stronger gravity
hook: Change gravitational acceleration and predict buoyant force.
misconception: buoyant force stays fixed when gravitational acceleration doubles.
objective: Apply F_b = ρgV to compare buoyant force when gravitational acceleration changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed volume submerged in fluid of fixed density, F_b = ρgV. When gravitational acceleration doubles, buoyant force becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F_b = ρgV; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed volume submerged in fluid of fixed density, with a nonzero initial result. If gravitational acceleration triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on buoyant force?
recall.why: Apply F_b = ρgV under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
